prerequisites: Successful completion of all other courses.

learning_outcomes.text: Students know how to apply acquired knowledge and problem-solving abilities in new environments within broader (or multidisciplinary) contexts related to their field of study.

Students are able to integrate knowledge and face the complexity of formulating judgments based on incomplete or limited information, including reflections on the social and ethical responsibilities linked to the application of their knowledge and judgments.
Students know how to communicate their conclusions and the ultimate knowledge and reasons that support them to specialized and non-specialized audiences clearly and unambiguously.
Students possess the learning skills that will allow them to continue studying in a largely self-directed or autonomous way.
To draft, scientifically interpret, and orally communicate, to specialized audiences, documents within the scope of the master's lines.
To apply the knowledge obtained in the master's degree to achieve greater efficiency, effectiveness, reliability, or safety in an industrial environment.
To use the acquired knowledge to maintain a critical and active attitude in the management of automation projects.
To effectively apply the competencies acquired in the master's degree in an individual work of medium complexity, including a report of said work and its defense before a tribunal.
Develop an application work in the field of automation or process supervision.
Acquire skills that allow for professional action as a member of an automation or supervision engineering team.
Apply and integrate with innovative, professional, and creative criteria the knowledge acquired for the preparation of a work within the scope of the master's objectives.
Defend, justify points of view, and critically reason the decisions made, as well as the results obtained in the work carried out.

syllabus_topics: Realization of an application project in the field of technologies seen throughout the master's degree, synthesizing and integrating the competencies acquired in the different subjects.

assessment_methods.method: Quality of the work, presentation, and provided documentation

Public and in-person (or remote) defense of the thesis, consisting of an exposition of its content or main lines, lasting approximately 20 minutes (15-30 minutes), followed by a Q&A session with the Evaluation Tribunal members.

assessment_rules: The Master's Thesis defense will be public and in-person (or remote), consisting of an exposition of its content or main lines, lasting approximately 20 minutes (not exceeding 30 minutes, nor less than 15 minutes). Subsequently, the student will answer questions and clarifications posed by the members of the Evaluation Tribunal. The Tribunal members will evaluate the quality of the work, the presentation, and the documentation, assigning a numerical grade from 0 to 10 and may propose 'Matrícula de Honor'.
